quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is easier to spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers can see you first. For example, if a blind corner is to your right, stay in the left part of your lane so drivers can spot you sooner.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Help you be seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane from other drivers, shows your intentions, helps avoid wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on slippery pavement. The front brake is safe on wet surfaces if you apply it slowly to prevent locking.

questions.question: Which sign is normally rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limits, are usually rectangular and white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times increases how visible you are to other drivers.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects your safety. It helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: Which of the following should NOT be checked before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Test both brakes to make sure the brake light turns on.
Check that the paint has no scratches.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint has no scratches.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition. Check oil and fluid levels. Test your low beam, high beam, taillight, turn signals, and brake light to make sure they all work.

questions.question: What is the best way to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: To be seen at an intersection, ride with your headlight on. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around you so you can move if needed. Do not rely on eye contact alone—a driver may not notice you even if they look at you.

questions.question: How do medications for headaches, colds, and hay fever usually affect you?
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety make you drowsy and may reduce your ability to ride safely. Always learn how a medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle may accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear without slowing down enough, the motorcycle will jerk suddenly and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts clearly. Always allow more space between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night than during the day.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: How can you increase how visible you are?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To increase visibility, wear bright colors or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle. Always use your turn signals. Flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other road users notice you.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with a driver means they will properly yield to you. Do not rely on eye contact alone for safety.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider safely returns to the original lane before beginning to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make things more dangerous by encouraging them to follow you faster.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that allows the arms to be exposed.
Shoes that stop below their ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you better grip on the controls.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people aren't used to using mirrors.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look closer than they really are.
It can be difficult to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you. They make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice with your mirrors to get used to them.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen with riders who have less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.question: The body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: To estimate how much alcohol remains, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.
